articles.title: War in the Middle East: latest developments
articles.summary: An Iranian missile strike on March 22 significantly damaged a kindergarten in Dimona, Israel, where a portrait of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was visible on a damaged wall. This incident clearly underscores the escalating military tensions and volatile geopolitical landscape between Iran and Israel, highlighting the direct impact of hostilities on civilian infrastructure and regional stability.

articles.title: How did Iran detect an ‘invisible’ F-35? Viral video points to a passive tracking system
articles.summary: An animated clip potentially solves the mystery of how Iran detected the F-35 stealth fighter, widely considered 'invisible.' This revelation is significant for defence, challenging the effectiveness of advanced stealth technology against emerging detection methods. Such developments are critical, as they prompt a re-evaluation of air superiority doctrines and global strategic assets.

articles.title: Indian Naval Ship Trikand concludes port call at Port Victoria in Seychelles
articles.summary: Indian Naval Ship (INS) Trikand, a stealth frigate, departed Port Victoria, Seychelles, on March 20, concluding a four-day port call. This visit strengthened bilateral ties and maritime cooperation between India and Seychelles, demonstrating India's commitment to regional security and stability in the Indian Ocean. Such deployments are crucial for projecting naval power and fostering diplomatic relations.

articles.title: Supply chains face 'hard lockdown' amid escalating West Asia conflict: Kotak Mahindra's Anindya Banerjee
articles.summary: India is currently prioritizing the management of its crude oil, CNG, and LPG supplies. This focus stems from significant global supply chain disruptions, intensified by escalating conflict in West Asia, which has imposed a "hard lockdown" on international energy flows. India is actively working to leverage its resources and strategies to mitigate these challenges and ensure domestic energy security amidst volatile international circumstances.

articles.title: US Northern Command Commander Labels Russia Primary Adversary, Cites Capabilities
articles.summary: U.S. Northern Command (NORTHCOM) chief, Gen. Gregory Guillot, has identified Russia as the primary threat to North America among all U.S. adversaries. He highlighted Russia's "greatest capability and capacity" to threaten the continent. This assessment underscores ongoing geopolitical tensions and the strategic importance of continental defense, providing critical insight into global security dynamics for SSB aspirants studying international relations and military strategy.

articles.title: Indian Navy warship Nilgiri joins Exercise KAKADU 2026 in Australia
articles.summary: Indian Navy frigate INS Nilgiri is participating in the sea phase of Exercise Kakadu 2026 in Australia, part of its Western Pacific deployment. This significant multinational exercise enhances interoperability and strengthens strategic ties between India and Australia. Such naval engagements demonstrate India's expanding maritime influence, commitment to regional security, and capability to operate effectively in diverse international waters.

articles.title: Overconfidence is how Wars are Lost – Viet-Iran?
articles.summary: This analysis argues wars are often lost in leaders' minds, not primarily on the battlefield, due to misjudgments of capabilities. For SSB aspirants, this highlights the paramount importance of strategic thinking, accurate assessment, and psychological resilience in military leadership. It underscores how understanding the mental dimension of conflict, beyond mere tactics, is crucial for sound decision-making and ultimate success.

articles.title: Ngwenya, Khoza appointed CEO and COO of World Cup 2027 Local Organising Committee
articles.summary: Qondisa Ngwenya has been appointed CEO and Edward Khoza COO for the Local Organising Committee (LOC) in Johannesburg. They will oversee the organisation of the upcoming ICC Men's cricket event. Their leadership is crucial for the successful execution of this major international tournament, managing all logistics and operations to ensure a world-class experience.

articles.title: Daily Mail: British nuclear-powered submarine with Tomahawk missiles in the Arabian Sea
articles.summary: A British nuclear-powered submarine, equipped with Tomahawk missiles, has been strategically deployed to the Arabian Sea. This positioning readies the vessel for potential long-range strikes, awaiting orders should international conflicts escalate further. The deployment underscores the UK's military presence and readiness to respond to global security challenges, emphasizing its role in maintaining stability in critical maritime regions.
